name: The Secret's Out
description: Someone's been digging into your history. How long you've really been in this game is about to become public knowledge.

chapters.title: Someone's Asking Questions
chapters.description: A blogger reached out. They're doing a profile piece on you. They want to know your story - when you started, where you came from, how long you've been in the game. They've already been asking around.

choices.label: Control the Story
choices.description: Sit down with them. Tell your story your way. They'll learn how long you've been in, but at least you frame it.

choices.label: Dodge the Questions
choices.description: Be vague. Give them enough for a story but nothing concrete about your timeline.

choices.label: No Comment
choices.description: Tell them you don't do interviews. Let them write whatever they want.

chapters.title: The Profile Drops
chapters.description: The article's out. It tells your real story - how long you've been grinding, where you started, the journey. People are reacting. Some are surprised by how new you are. Others respect the rapid rise.

choices.label: Embrace the Underdog Story
choices.description: Lean into it. 'Yeah I'm new. And I'm already here.'

choices.label: Show Your Maturity
choices.description: The timeline doesn't matter. Your skill does. Keep proving that.

chapters.title: They Found Out Anyway
chapters.description: The blogger dug deeper. Old clips, forum posts, interviews. They pieced together your actual timeline. Now they're running the story as 'The Mystery Behind [Your Name]' - and speculating about why you hid it.

choices.label: Set the Record Straight
choices.description: Post your own statement. 'Since people are talking, here's the truth.'

choices.label: Go After the Blogger
choices.description: Call them out for invading your privacy. Make it about their behavior, not yours.

chapters.title: The Hit Piece
chapters.description: The blogger didn't appreciate being stonewalled. The article is up: 'Who Is [Your Name] Really?' They're questioning everything - your skills, your wins, your authenticity. Comments are brutal.

choices.label: Respond With Fire
choices.description: Clap back publicly. Expose their bias. Turn it into beef.

choices.label: Ignore It
choices.description: Don't engage. Let it die. Focus on your next battle.

chapters.title: The Narrative Shifts
chapters.description: Your statement helped. People understand why you kept it private - nobody wants to be judged by years instead of skill. Some still think you're hiding something, but most moved on.

choices.label: Use It As Fuel
choices.description: Let it motivate your next battle. Show them time doesn't equal talent.

choices.label: Move Past It
choices.description: It's public now. Nothing left to hide. Just keep working.

chapters.title: Blogger Beef
chapters.description: The blogger's clapping back. They're posting receipts, old screenshots, calling you paranoid. It's becoming a thing. Other battlers are picking sides. Your opponent next week is watching closely.

choices.label: End the Beef
choices.description: It's not worth it. Tell them you're done engaging. Focus on battles.

choices.label: Escalate
choices.description: You're not backing down. Bar them up. Make it personal.

chapters.title: Battle Lines Drawn
chapters.description: Your response got attention. The blogger has supporters, but so do you. Other battlers are using your beef in their bars. Your career length is public now, but the conversation shifted to your realness.

choices.label: Let the Next Battle Speak
choices.description: End the debate by performing. Haters can't argue with a body.

choices.label: Keep the Smoke
choices.description: This beef is good publicity. Keep your name in conversations.

endings.title: The Underdog
endings.description: Your career length is public knowledge now, but the story is positive. You're the underdog who rose fast. Newcomers look up to you. Veterans respect the hustle.

endings.title: Earned Respect
endings.description: Nobody cares about your timeline anymore. They care about your battles. Your career length is public but irrelevant - your skill speaks for itself.

endings.title: Motivated
endings.description: The exposure lit a fire. You're training harder, writing more, performing better. Your career length is out there, but you're making sure the numbers next to it keep growing.

endings.title: Fresh Start
endings.description: No more secrets. It's freeing, actually. You don't have to be careful about what you say in interviews. The pressure of keeping it hidden is gone.

endings.title: Unbothered
endings.description: You didn't engage with the drama. Your career length is public now, but you didn't give anyone the satisfaction of a reaction. Some respect it, some think you're hiding more.

endings.title: Peace Made
endings.description: You ended the beef before it got ugly. The blogger moved on to other targets. Your career is public, the drama is dead. Life continues.

endings.title: Statement Performance
endings.description: You let your battle speak. And it spoke loudly. Your career length doesn't matter when you're bodying people. The haters are quiet now.

endings.title: Notorious
endings.description: You're known for the beef now. Not necessarily bad - any publicity is publicity. But every interview will ask about it. Your career length is public, and so is your willingness to go to war.

endings.title: At War
endings.description: You're in a full-blown beef with media now. Other bloggers are taking sides. It's affecting your bookings - some leagues don't want the drama. Your career length is old news, but the conflict isn't.
